newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down on Tuesday on a technical correction following Monday's rise helped by selling from retail investors, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 3,370 yuan ($406) per tonne, losing six yuan. It opened at 3,370 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,378 and a low of 3,350.
July fell eight to 3,390, September 25 to 3,385 and November 20 to 3,400.
Combined volume rose to 15,800 tonnes from 11,600.
Soybeans opened lower on a correction and moved at low levels for most of the session with retail investors dominating the day's trading given a lack of market-moving news, traders said.
"Thin volume indicates a lack of institutional investors and soybeans will not rise or fall sharply in the short term," one trader said.
Analysts expected soybeans to continue to move in a narrow range over the next few days.
